adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed() combined with a stable Stream.sorted() means providers that tie on order() (e.g. a broken deployment that ships both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider, both order()=200) are resolved purely by ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order, which is JVM/classloader/deployment-dependent and unspecified, so which provider "wins" (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) can silently differ across otherwise-identical environments with no distinguishing log line

adjudication.rationale: In CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(), providers are now loaded via ServiceLoader and sorted only by order() descending (".sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed())"). The diff also changes behavior from throwing when multiple providers are present to silently selecting foundProviders.get(0) and only debug-logging the rest. Since multiple built-in providers in this diff return the same order() value (DefaultCryptoProvider=200, WildFlyElytronProvider=200, FIPS1402Provider=200), ties are resolved purely by ServiceLoader iteration order, which is not specified and can vary by classpath/classloader/deployment. This makes the chosen crypto provider potentially non-deterministic across environments with no clear warning, which can impact correctness/security (e.g., FIPS vs non-FIPS selection).

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Encoder, `concatenate(ASN1Encoder... objects)` indeed has default (package-private) access and is only called by `writeDerSeq(...)` within the same class, so it could be made `private`. However, this is purely an encapsulation/style suggestion and not a defect or substantial review issue evidenced by the diff.
